name: Dehu
catalog_quote: [record] In Dehu stress is non-phonemic, having only a demarkative function. It indicates the division between words. ... Primary stress always falls on the first syllable of the word. With compound words, both elements have a primary stress, this being true also of reduplicatives. ... Secondary stress always occurs, in polysyllabic words, on the third syllable. audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.recode_to: (none mandatory) If catalog policy codes instrumentally-refuted impressionistic stress as 'no word stress / right-edge phrasal prominence' (as for French/Korean-type edge-marking languages), Dehu is a candidate for that class on the strength of Torres et al. 2018, Torres & Fletcher 2020, 2022; otherwise keep fixed-dominant (initial) with not in the strict set as now.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding Tryon 1968 §1.1 passage is verbatim at pp. 1-2 of the PL-B7 text we hold/PDF, and the Torres & Fletcher 2022 fragment is verbatim at p. 6 of the Glossa PDF we hold; but the record's formal quote/cite/loc/grade fields are empty (the material sits only in the domain quotation/the domain locator), so the evidence fields should be populated from the copy we hold. (2) Deciding source: a 1968 Pacific Linguistics grammar (xi+111 pp), primary and first-hand, agreeing (per Torres & Fletcher's summaries) with Lenormand 1954; the StressTyp2 fifth-syllable error was already corrected against it. sources.citation: Torres, Catalina & Janet Fletcher. 2020. The alignment of F0 tonal targets under changes in speech rate in Drehu. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 147(4): 2947-2958. doi:10.1121/10.0001006 (author-posted copy).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p. 2948: 'According to Lenormand (1954), stress (accent d'intensite), always falls on the first syllable of a word ... when words obtain a prefix, the stress pattern remains and main stress shifts to the inserted first syllable ... Tryon (1968a) proposes secondary stress in polysyllabic words, with it always falling on the third syllable'. Conclusion: 'it is proposed that Drehu shows an edge prominence marking system with an initial L tone and a prominence lending H tone at the right edge of the prosodic word. ... Contrary to earlier impressionistic accounts (Lenormand, 1954; Tryon, 1968a), th
sources.locator: §I p. 2948 (summary of Lenormand 1954 / Tryon 1968) and §VI Conclusion p. 2955-2956
sources.note: Non-focal NPs at two speech rates; concludes phrasal L..H edge marking rather than lexical stress; now obtained by the project (author copy).

sources.citation: Torres, Catalina, Janet Fletcher & Gillian Wigglesworth. 2018. Investigating word prominence in Drehu. Proceedings of the 17th Australasian International Conference on Speech Science and Technology (SST 2018), 141-144.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Previous descriptions of Drehu phonology claimed that the language has initial word stress. ... Contrary to our predictions, it was found that vowel duration was significantly longer on the final syllable of target tokens. Similarly, a rise was often observed, which in 97.6% of the cases ended on a peak at the right edge of the constituent. ... the lack of any durational or tonal cues associated with word-initial syllables calls for a further investigation, and a revaluation of previous stress analyses of Drehu' (4 female speakers, words in informational focus).
sources.note: First acoustic test of the initial-stress claim (no durational/tonal cue on initial syllables; final-syllable lengthening and right-edge F0 peak); now obtained by the project.
